summary:
Subcarpathian Voivodeship stands under the national framework of Poland, which carries the country's entry rules, custody conditions, document and marker rules, and hate-crime measures; the findings below are those specific to the voivodeship.

On 20 September 2021 the Podkarpackie voivodeship council repealed its 'LGBT-free' resolution and replaced the ordinance with a generic anti-discrimination statement. The county-level layer ended later: on 27 April 2025 the county of Łańcut, in the voivodeship's southeast, repealed its anti-LGBT resolution at an extraordinary councillors' session, the last local authority in Poland to do so.

No region-specific enforcement action, prosecution, healthcare restriction, facility rule or trans-specific incident in Subcarpathian Voivodeship is documented in the available sources. For those matters the national assessment applies.
tangentialFactors: The voivodeship's repeal followed a threat by the European Commission to withhold regional development funds, and Podkarpackie acted alongside Małopolska and Lubelskie in the same move. The Atlas of Hate mapping project estimated that at the peak of the wave about one third of Poland's territory was covered by such documents, which places the voivodeship's declarations within a country-wide pattern rather than a local peculiarity.
localsOnly: Both measures were acts of local government rather than of the national legislature, so their repeal changed the official posture of the voivodeship and of Łańcut county without altering national law. Residents of the voivodeship are subject to the same local-authority decisions as visitors; the sources record no separate resident-facing provision.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not record whether the repealed resolutions carried any binding effect on services, employment or facilities in the voivodeship.

No region-specific record of hate-crime prosecution, policing practice, healthcare access or trans-specific violence in Podkarpackie was identified.

Whether any local authority in the voivodeship has adopted a replacement measure beyond the generic anti-discrimination statement is not sourced.
